description: VRPy is a Python framework for solving vehicle-routing problems by column generation. Users describe customers, depots and arcs in a NetworkX directed graph, set costs, times, demands and vehicle limits, and run the solver to obtain route sets and an objective value. Its documented variants include capacitated routing, time windows, simultaneous delivery and collection, resource limits, and heterogeneous fleets. Spatial coverage is whatever road or logistics network a user encodes; the package does not provide a road dataset or a fixed historical period. Its repository, package instructions and examples are public under MIT. The tool can support freight or service-fleet capacity studies, compare delivery routes after a disruption, or create operational inputs for a wider transport simulation. The result depends on the chosen graph, travel costs and constraints. A solved mathematical route does not establish vehicle behaviour under traffic, driver regulations or uncertain demand. No directly related catalogue record was established by the comparison. This review read the JOSS article page, repository metadata and README, but did not install VRPy or solve an instance.
